newsitem.title: USA: Blood protein could lead to an Alzheimer's test.
newsitem.headline: Blood protein could lead to an Alzheimer's test.

text.p: A Canadian doctor on Tuesday reported finding a protein that is elevated in the blood of people with Alzheimer's disease, a finding that could someday lead to a test to diagnose the incurable dementia.
In the November edition of the journal Nature Medicine, Dr. Wilfred Jefferies of the University of British Columbia reported that the iron binding protein p97 is higher in people with Alzheimer's.
The findings are very preliminary, but could be useful both in eventually developing a diagnostic test, in monitoring the course of disease and possibly in testing potential therapies for Alzheimers.

"A simple and reliable laboratory test for the detection of AD, such as a biochemical marker that could be ideally detected in blood, would be a valuable tool in both the assessment and management of the disease," he wrote.
Alzheimers cannot be definitively diagnosed until autopsy, although clinical examination can help doctors distinguish Alzheimer's from other dementia, some of which can be treated.
